svg.title: ithalat trackpad wiring (magnetic pogo)
svg.desc: Azoteq TPS65 trackpad joins the Yakamoz OLED I2C1 bus (GP2/GP3). Recommended, with no case modification: 4-5 x 30 AWG wires from tap A (the OLED module header joints or the switchplate TB1 socket, same nets as Pico pins 4, 5, 36, 38) or tap B (the Pico pins themselves; RDY always from Pico pin 20) run flat over the switchplate, under the OLED cover, into the printed dock's rear channel and a 5-pin magnetic pogo receptacle (1 SDA, 2 3V3, 3 GND, 4 SCL, 5 RDY). The magnetic plug on a short pigtail goes to the TPS65 2.0 mm solder pads. Alternative that modifies the case: the main-PCB OL1 holes under the switchplate, which need a notch filed in an internal acrylic bar. The USB-C connector variant is drawn in wiring-usbc.svg.
svg.text: ithalat trackpad wiring, magnetic pogo: TPS65 on the OLED's I2C1 bus
4 wires required (SDA, SCL, 3V3, GND) + optional RDY. Connector pinout, identical on both halves: 1 SDA · 2 3V3 · 3 GND · 4 SCL · 5 RDY
R1/R2: pull-ups on the main PCB (bottom side)
under the OLED cover → dock rear channel
RDY (optional): solder at Pico pin 20 / GP15, not on any header
Tap B: or solder the four wires to Pico pins 4, 5, 36, 38
No case modification either way: only the OLED cover comes off.
then up through the plug bay
Tap A, top view: OLED header · TB1 socket
TB1: plug in a 5-pin male header, no soldering.
Not keyed: mark the GND end. Before power-up,
red must beep to Pico 36 and black to Pico 38.
same order below the OLED; acrylic bar must be filed.
thin line = PCB trace · thick line = wire
• 3.3 V only, never 5 V / VBUS (TPS65 max 3.6 V)
• OLED 0x3C + TPS65 0x74 share I2C1: no clash
• Tap B: Pico pins · alt.: main-PCB OL1 (case mod)
• Safest: (un)plug the pad with USB disconnected
